sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Grant County, KY?
sections.html:
A Grant County tax bill passes through three counters. The PVA decides what each parcel is worth. The sheriff takes payment on the current year. The county clerk picks up whatever is still open after mid-April. Rates come from the levying bodies themselves: the fiscal court, the school system, and any city or special district that taxes the parcel.

Find the PVA in the courthouse at 101 North Main Street in Williamstown, or call (859) 824-6511. The sheriff's office is at 212 Barnes Road, Suite A, with posted weekday hours of 8 to 4 and a main number of (859) 824-3333. Checks can be mailed to PO Box 235, Dry Ridge, KY 41035. The county directory sends delinquent-bill questions to the clerk at (859) 824-3321.

City tax bills never go through the sheriff. Williamstown, Dry Ridge, Corinth and Crittenden each bill their own, so a municipal charge on a closing statement is a question for that city hall.

sections.h2: What is the payment calendar for a Grant County tax bill?
sections.html:
The sheriff mails bills and posts them online on October 1, then takes payment until April 15. Splitting a bill into two installments is not allowed. Cards work, with a processing charge from the card company, and a mail-in payer who wants a receipt encloses a stamped return envelope.

Grant County Sheriff's posted schedule for current-year bills (source: Grant County Sheriff's Office, tax collection page)
Payment madeResult
Oct. 1 through Nov. 1Two percent off the bill
Nov. 2 through Dec. 31Bill at face value
All of JanuaryFive percent added
Feb. 1 through Apr. 15Twenty-one percent added, as posted
After Apr. 15County Clerk takes over the bill

The state law behind this calendar, KRS 134.015, sets a 10 percent penalty for anything paid after January. The sheriff's 21 percent figure for February through April 15 is higher, so ask for an itemized payoff in writing before you sign a contract that depends on it.

sections.h2: Why did my Grant County tax bill arrive in the seller's name?
sections.html:
The sheriff bills whoever was listed as owner on January 1. Buy in spring and the year's first bill still carries the previous owner's name. The sheriff does not receive deed transfers, so the seller has to hand the bill over.

  • Write the split of that year's bill into the purchase agreement, since the county does not apportion it.
  • Put the buyer's in-care-of address on the deed, a required item under KRS 382.135.
  • After recording, call the PVA and confirm the mailing address now on file.

When a closing agent pays the open bill out of the seller's proceeds, the settlement statement should show it as its own line.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Grant County assessment?
sections.html:
No appeal can be filed until you have sat down with the PVA or a deputy, so the office is your first stop. Then comes a 13-day public viewing of the roll, starting the first Monday of May.

  • At the conference, the PVA walks through the method behind your value and keeps a written record.
  • Deliver the written appeal to the Clerk before closing time the day after the inspection window shuts.
  • Collect proof: nearby sales, contractor bids, photos of damage, insurance papers, cost of construction.
  • Attend the board hearing, which falls within five weeks of the window closing. A no-show forfeits further review by the state Claims Commission.

An appeal without documents is denied by the board. Should bills go out before the board decides, your own figure is billed for now. A higher final value brings a second bill for the difference.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption in Grant County?
sections.html:
Yes. Owners aged 65 or more, or totally disabled, may subtract $49,100 from assessed value for 2025-2026. A Grant County house assessed at $250,000 would be taxed on $200,900.

Applications are made at the PVA, and the sheriff's office refers anyone asking about it there. Acceptable proof of age includes a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability filers renew yearly, with two groups spared that chore: veterans rated service-connected, and anyone holding a permanent-disability finding from Social Security or the state retirement system.

Tell the PVA when you sell, so the deduction comes off the old address and the new owner can apply on their own.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Grant County taxes when I sell?
sections.html:
The debt stays attached to the parcel. The sheriff handles only the current year, so once a bill crosses April 15 it lands in the Clerk's office with a lien recorded against the property. A buyer inherits the lien, which can last 11 years (KRS 134.420).

Costs climb in steps. In the Department of Revenue's worked example, a $1,000 bill reaches the Clerk as a $1,254 certificate. Paid after the county attorney's first notice, that figure grows to $1,611.30 once monthly interest, two commissions, postage and a $10 lien fee are added.

The Clerk may auction the certificate between 90 and 135 days after transfer, and the winning bidder can tack on more charges. Have the Clerk quote a payoff before the house goes on the market. A cash buyer can pay the lien off at closing, with the balance taken from the price.

sections.h2: What should a Grant County seller know about the county itself?
sections.html:
Grant County lies in northern Kentucky inside the Cincinnati metropolitan area. It was carved from Pendleton County in 1820 and has 258 square miles of land. Williamstown holds the courthouse, while Dry Ridge, Corinth and Crittenden complete the list of cities. Families here send children to Grant County Schools or to Williamstown Independent Schools, and the Ark Encounter in Williamstown brings in visitors from across the region.

Growth is the main story here. The census counted 9,999 residents in 1970, 22,384 in 2000 and 24,941 in 2020, and the 1939 courthouse in Williamstown has since been joined by a judicial center that opened in April 2010. Census QuickFacts reports:

  • 26,181 residents in 2025, a 5.0 percent rise from the 2020 base.
  • A median owner-occupied home value of $209,500 and a 75.1 percent ownership rate.
  • Median household income of $69,178 and a mean commute of 26.9 minutes.
  • Median gross rent of $862 and 110 building permits in 2025.

A cash purchase closes as-is, which can suit an owner with repairs waiting or a balance outstanding.

faqs.q: Who takes property tax payments in Grant County, KY?
faqs.a: The sheriff's office, at 212 Barnes Road, Suite A in Williamstown, or by mail to PO Box 235, Dry Ridge. Bills left unpaid after April 15 are collected by the County Clerk.

faqs.q: What is the last day for the early-payment discount in Grant County?
faqs.a: November 1. A two percent reduction applies if the whole bill is paid between October 1 and that date, and the bill returns to face value from November 2.

faqs.q: Can a Grant County tax bill be paid in two installments?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff requires full payment of each bill, so pick a payment window you can cover in one go.

faqs.q: How large is the homestead deduction for a Grant County house?
faqs.a: $49,100 for 2025-2026, taken off the assessed value. Applicants must be 65 or over, or totally disabled, and file with the PVA at (859) 824-6511.

faqs.q: Must back taxes be settled before I list a Grant County house?
faqs.a: They can wait until closing, since the lien follows the parcel and gets paid from the sale. Phone the Clerk at (859) 824-3321 for a payoff figure so your title agent can plan around it.
